title: Armond White —maybe the greatest living critic?

commenti.body: [removed]
[removed]

His prose is entertaining but his insights are for the most part incredibly shallow and predictable, because all of his opinions derive foremost from his obnoxious contrarianism and ironically a quite conservative and limited outlook. He has an axe to grind against the critical establishment in film, has publicly embarrassed himself at awards shows, and is generally a self-aggrandizing blowhard, and he is that both in person and in writing. 

Like so many of those who challenge the mainstream for no particular useful purpose than just to challenge the mainstream - the Graham Hancocks of the world - there’s just almost no actual value to be found there. The idea in going against the grain is to have a meaningful alternative to offer, not simply to lash out impotently. 

But Armond White’s use of language is pretty strong.
Pretty sure he's just a contrarian. No living human being could have such consistently opposite opinions unless it was an active choice to do so. Not worth anyone's time to read his flame bait.

These are far from his best days now that he can't watch a Hollywood movie without seeing the specter of Hillary Clinton haunting it, but before 2016 caused him to eat his own brain, he was often genuinely insightful and would go to bat for filmmakers no one else would.

I actually stopped paying attention to him years before (?) this political turn happened in his writing, but did he ever explain, preferably in one place/piece, what made him become a Hilary-hating conspiracy theorist?  I mean, I don't even know if that sums it up....I stopped reading him after I realized most of what I was getting was rhetoric and trolling.  Maybe my own loss.

I don't know. He was always conservative. (Along some dimensions. He's queer after all.) And he's always been a provocateur. And he's always been conspiracy-minded, thinking that film critics and Hollywood and left-wing politics are too cozy with one another. (Someone of his best pieces are on this, frankly. For instance, on Denby breaking the Fincher embargo.) As time went on he just got ruder and more hostile, leading to him isolating himself, getting kicked out of the New York Critics circle in 2014. He was in a perfect place to get swept up into the Fox News tornado as he aged.
Thanks for the reply.  Sorry to ask you to do my footwork for me, but what White piece in particular are you referencing re: Denby/Fincher?

I recently spent the night going through some of his recent reviews at the National Review after realizing he had written essays for the Criterion Collection in the past. They were not good. He seemed to just make wild accusations without ever backing them up. I love a good criticism of Hollywood, of Star Wars, but there's a difference between Mark Fisher and Star Wars Theory. Armond just seems to be pumping reviews out, with a predetermined take down in mind.

\>has publicly embarrassed himself at awards shows

  
Link please lol
I think he hits the nail at times though
That might be true, I mostly read him on movies I dislike but most people like and without fail he expresses my emotions better than I could have.

Lo and behold, White made a better version of my own post:



\>We got film critics who are employed professionally by legitimate publications, and we have the world of the internet film writers. The internet has become so pervasive and overwhelming that the internet has stolen the impact and prestige and effect that traditional professional film criticism used to have. As a result of that I think that people who are now employed by the mainstream media are so intimidated by the internet that it seems, when you read mainstream published film critics, that they've simply given up being film critics, because they're afraid of losing readership, because they're afraid of losing their jobs, probably because publishers and editors simply want to get readers and appease readers, rather than inform and instruct readers. And I think that leads to a kind of anarchy where there are very few people writing about film who know what they're talking about and who are rigorous about having standards in film. The anarchy, I think, comes from the the fact that in mainstream media and the internet, most people who are writing about films are simply writing from a fan's perspective instead of a truly critical perspective. So what used to be termed "film critics" now is almost meaningless, because you just got a free-for-all of enthusiasms rather than criticism
Not enough to qualify as the greatest living critic.
Who would it be then for you?

He’s just an attention seeker. He doesn’t seem to really understand whatever it is that he’s watching. He goes into the film with a fixed opinion and he ignores what he’s seeing. The definition of a bad critic.

\>He doesn’t seem to really understand whatever it is that he’s watching.

  
Do you have a review which is like this? In my estimation he gets the form on a level very few people do and his reviews always make sense even if I don't agree.

He may say that, but it’s typical trolling. He knows what to say to reel you in. That’s all. When it comes down to whether or not he actually has these profound critical insights, he doesn’t go deeper than anyone else.
I’m too old to care who’s living or dead.
Isn't that a concession lol
